about.title: About ToolkitLife
about.lead: ToolkitLife is a free collection of browser-based tools and calculators. Open a tool, get an answer in seconds, and leave - no account, no signup, no email.
about.sections.0.title: How it works
about.sections.0.paragraphs.0: Every tool runs entirely in your browser with JavaScript and WebAssembly. Files you process stay on your device: images, videos, audio, and text are never uploaded to a server. That is why the tools are fast, private, and free to operate.
about.sections.1.title: Privacy by design
about.sections.1.paragraphs.0: Because nothing is uploaded, we cannot see, store, or sell your data. The site uses only anonymous, aggregated analytics to understand which tools are useful. See our Privacy Policy for details.
about.sections.2.title: What's inside
about.sections.2.paragraphs.0: The toolbox covers financial, health, and legal calculators; marketing and webmaster utilities; text and code converters; and image, video, and audio tools - including AI features that run locally with on-device models. Every tool is available in five languages: English, 简体中文, 日本語, 한국어, and Русский.
about.sections.2.paragraphs.1: Financial, health, and legal calculators are provided for general information only and include a disclaimer: they are estimates, not professional advice.

tools.ai-image-detector.metadata.title: AI Image Detector - Check If an Image Is AI Generated
tools.ai-image-detector.metadata.descrip: Detect AI-generated images in your browser. Checks C2PA credentials, generator signatures (Midjourney, DALL-E, SynthID), metadata & anomalies. 100% local.
tools.ai-image-detector.title: AI Image Detector
tools.ai-image-detector.description: Check if an image was AI-generated — C2PA credentials, generator signatures, metadata, and frequency analysis. Everything runs locally in your browser; images are never uploaded.
tools.ai-image-detector.faqs.0.question: How does the AI image detector work?
tools.ai-image-detector.faqs.0.answer: It runs four checks in your browser: C2PA / Content Credentials verification (the strongest signal), AI generator signatures in metadata (Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, DALL-E, SynthID, etc.), structured metadata, and byte-level frequency anomalies that synthetic images often leave behind.
tools.ai-image-detector.faqs.1.question: Are my images uploaded to a server?
tools.ai-image-detector.faqs.1.answer: No. Every check runs entirely in your browser. The image never leaves your device — there is no upload and no server-side processing.
tools.ai-image-detector.faqs.2.question: Can the detector prove an image is AI-generated?
tools.ai-image-detector.faqs.2.answer: Not with certainty. Detection is probabilistic. C2PA credentials that state an AI source are strong evidence, but metadata can be stripped and frequency analysis is a heuristic. Treat the verdict as one signal, not proof.
tools.ai-image-detector.faqs.3.question: What image formats are supported?
tools.ai-image-detector.faqs.3.answer: JPEG, PNG, and WebP. These are the formats that carry the metadata and byte-level signatures the detector looks for.
tools.ai-image-detector.faqs.4.question: Why does my AI-generated image show no signals?
tools.ai-image-detector.faqs.4.answer: Many generators strip metadata, and some AI images are statistically very close to natural ones. If no signal is found, the tool reports "No AI-generation signal found" — that is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.
tools.ai-image-detector.guide.heading: How to use:
tools.ai-image-detector.guide.steps.0: Drop or select a JPEG, PNG, or WebP image. It is analyzed entirely on your device.
tools.ai-image-detector.guide.steps.1: Click "Analyze Image". The tool checks C2PA credentials, AI generator signatures, metadata, and pixel frequency.
tools.ai-image-detector.guide.steps.2: Read the verdict and evidence cards. C2PA verification is the strongest signal; frequency analysis is heuristic.
tools.ai-image-detector.ui.hint: JPEG · PNG · WebP — processed locally, never uploaded
tools.ai-image-detector.ui.disclaimer: Disclaimer: Detection is probabilistic, not proof. A clean result does not guarantee an image is human-made, and a flagged result is one signal among several. C2PA credentials are the strongest evidence.
tools.ai-image-detector.verdict.unsuitab: Image not suitable for frequency analysis
tools.ai-image-detector.descs.c2pa.aiVer: The C2PA / Content Credentials manifest confirms this image was produced by an AI model.
tools.ai-image-detector.descs.c2pa.inval: A C2PA manifest exists but fails validation — it may have been tampered with.
tools.ai-image-detector.descs.c2pa.verif: A valid C2PA manifest confirms a non-AI digital source (camera capture or manual creation).
tools.ai-image-detector.descs.c2pa.struc: C2PA/JUMBF structures are present; validation could not fully confirm the source.
tools.ai-image-detector.descs.c2pa.bytes: Byte-level hints of C2PA markers were found without a complete manifest.
tools.ai-image-detector.descs.c2pa.notfo: No C2PA / Content Credentials markers were found in the file.
tools.ai-image-detector.descs.metadata.h: Image metadata directly records an AI generation tool or marker.
tools.ai-image-detector.descs.metadata.p: Metadata fields were extracted but none match AI-generation markers.
tools.ai-image-detector.descs.metadata.e: The image carries almost no metadata (possibly stripped).
Byte distribution deviates from natural images — possible invisible watermark.
Byte distribution looks natural; no watermark anomaly detected.
tools.ai-object-eraser.metadata.title: AI Object Eraser - Remove Objects from Photos Online
tools.ai-object-eraser.metadata.descript: Remove unwanted objects, people, or text from photos with AI in your browser. Click to select, erase in seconds. Free, no upload, 100% private.
tools.ai-object-eraser.title: AI Object Eraser
tools.ai-object-eraser.description: Remove unwanted objects, people, or text from a photo with a few clicks. AI selects the object you click on, then regenerates the area so it disappears cleanly. Everything runs locally in your browser.
tools.ai-object-eraser.faqs.0.question: How does the AI object eraser work?
tools.ai-object-eraser.faqs.0.answer: Two AI models run inside your browser. First, a Segment Anything model finds the exact pixels of the object you click on. Then an inpainting model regenerates that area using the surrounding colors and textures, so the object disappears cleanly.
tools.ai-object-eraser.faqs.1.question: Is my photo uploaded to a server?
tools.ai-object-eraser.faqs.1.answer: No. Every AI model and all image processing run entirely in your browser with WebAssembly. Your photo never leaves your device and nothing is stored.
tools.ai-object-eraser.faqs.2.question: What can I remove from a photo?
tools.ai-object-eraser.faqs.2.answer: Anything you can click on: people, animals, cars, watermarks, text, cables, reflections, and other unwanted objects. Objects with a clear boundary and fairly uniform surroundings produce the cleanest result.
tools.ai-object-eraser.faqs.3.question: Is this tool free?
tools.ai-object-eraser.faqs.3.answer: Yes — free with no signup, no watermarks, and no usage limits. The first run downloads the AI models (about 120 MB), which are then cached in your browser for future use.
tools.ai-object-eraser.faqs.4.question: Why does the first use take longer?
tools.ai-object-eraser.faqs.4.answer: The first time, the AI models are downloaded and the image encoder takes a few seconds to prepare your photo. After that, selecting and erasing take only seconds.
tools.ai-object-eraser.upload.drop: Drop a photo or click to upload
tools.ai-object-eraser.upload.formats: PNG, JPG, WEBP — longest edge up to 4096px
tools.ai-object-eraser.status.pendingAna: Ready — click “Analyze image” to load the AI model
tools.ai-object-eraser.status.segmentSta: Click on the object you want to remove
tools.ai-object-eraser.status.segmentHin: Keep clicking to refine — the magenta overlay is what will be erased
tools.ai-object-eraser.errors.read: Sorry, this image could not be read. Try another file.
tools.ai-object-eraser.errors.analyze: The AI model failed to load. Please check your connection and try again.
tools.ai-object-eraser.errors.decode: Could not segment that point. Click on the object again.
tools.ai-object-eraser.errors.erase: Erasing failed. Try a different selection or a smaller area.
tools.ai-object-eraser.errors.noPoints: First click on the object you want to remove.
tools.ai-object-eraser.modelNote: The first run downloads an AI model (~118 MB, one-time, cached in your browser) and analyzes your photo locally. Nothing is uploaded.
tools.ai-object-eraser.guide.whatIs.titl: What Is the AI Object Eraser?
tools.ai-object-eraser.guide.whatIs.body: The AI Object Eraser removes unwanted objects, people, text, or watermarks from a photo. Click the object you want gone, and two AI models — a Segment Anything segmentation model and an MI-GAN inpainting model — select it precisely and regenerate the area behind it.
Both models run entirely in your browser using WebAssembly, so the tool is free, unlimited, and private: your photos never leave your device.
tools.ai-object-eraser.guide.howTo.title: How to Erase an Object from a Photo
tools.ai-object-eraser.guide.howTo.items: Upload or drop a photo onto the page.
Click “Analyze image”. On the first run the AI models are downloaded and cached — this happens only once.
Click on the object you want to remove. Each click adds to the selection (green dots).
If the selection includes background you want to keep, hold Shift and click it (red dot) to exclude it.
Keep adding points until the magenta overlay covers the whole object, then click “Erase Object”.
Wait a few seconds, compare the before and after, and download the result as a PNG.
tools.ai-object-eraser.guide.tips.title: Tips for the Best Results
Objects with clean edges surrounded by fairly uniform background erase most convincingly.
Click on the center of the object first — that gives the AI the clearest signal about what to select.
For very large objects, erase in two passes: remove one part, then click the remaining part on the fresh result.
In complex scenes, hold Shift and click background areas that get wrongly selected to keep them intact.
tools.what-is-my-browser.metadata.title: What Is My Browser
tools.what-is-my-browser.metadata.descri: Detect your browser name, version, OS and IP address
tools.what-is-my-browser.faqs.0.question: How does this detect my browser?
tools.what-is-my-browser.faqs.0.answer: The tool reads your browser's User-Agent string and other JavaScript APIs available to any website.
tools.what-is-my-browser.faqs.1.question: Is my data sent anywhere?
tools.what-is-my-browser.faqs.1.answer: No. Everything is detected locally in your browser, except your public IP which is requested from a public IP service.
tools.what-is-my-browser.faqs.2.question: Why does my browser matter for websites?
tools.what-is-my-browser.faqs.2.answer: Websites use browser detection to deliver compatible features, and your User-Agent helps developers test and debug their sites.
tools.what-is-my-browser.guide.intro.par: This tool detects your browser name, version, rendering engine, operating system, screen resolution, language, timezone and public IP address.
Open the page and the information is detected automatically. Click Refresh to re-detect after changing settings.
The User-Agent string is shown at the bottom for developers.
Copy the User-Agent to share it when reporting a bug.
If you use a VPN, the IP shown may belong to your VPN provider instead of your real location.

tools.geo-ip-locator.faqs.0.question: How accurate is IP geolocation?
tools.geo-ip-locator.faqs.0.answer: IP geolocation typically identifies the city or region level. It is not exact to a physical address.
tools.geo-ip-locator.faqs.1.question: Can IP location be wrong?
tools.geo-ip-locator.faqs.1.answer: Yes. VPNs, proxies and mobile carriers can make an IP appear in a different location than you actually are.
tools.geo-ip-locator.faqs.2.question: What is an ASN?
tools.geo-ip-locator.faqs.2.answer: An Autonomous System Number identifies the network that owns the IP block, usually an ISP or hosting company.

tools.redirect-checker.metadata.title: Redirect Checker
tools.redirect-checker.metadata.descript: Check where a URL redirects to and its final status code
tools.redirect-checker.labels.hasRedirec: This URL redirects to another address
tools.redirect-checker.messages.fetchFai: Could not fetch the URL. The site may block automated requests or the URL may be invalid.
tools.redirect-checker.messages.disclaim: This is a lightweight check performed through a proxy. For full redirect chains, use a server-side tool.
tools.redirect-checker.faqs.0.question: What is a 301 redirect?
tools.redirect-checker.faqs.0.answer: A 301 redirect permanently points an old URL to a new one, telling browsers and search engines the page has moved.
tools.redirect-checker.faqs.1.question: Why should I check redirects?
tools.redirect-checker.faqs.1.answer: Broken or long redirect chains slow down your site and can hurt SEO. Checking helps you keep links healthy.
tools.redirect-checker.faqs.2.question: What status codes matter?
tools.redirect-checker.faqs.2.answer: 200 means OK, 301/302 mean redirected, 404 means not found, and 403/500 indicate errors.
tools.redirect-checker.guide.intro.title: What is a Redirect Checker?
tools.redirect-checker.guide.intro.parag: A redirect checker tests a URL to see if it redirects to another address and shows the final destination and status code.
Enter the URL and click Check. The tool fetches the URL through a proxy and compares the final URL with the original.
If the final URL differs, the page is being redirected.
The status code tells you if the page is healthy (200) or moved (301/302).
After moving pages, always set up 301 redirects from old URLs to preserve SEO value.
tools.is-it-down.metadata.title: Is It Down
tools.is-it-down.metadata.description: Check if a website is down for everyone or just you
tools.is-it-down.messages.disclaimer: This checks reachability through a proxy. A site may still be down for you due to local network issues, or up for you while down elsewhere.
tools.is-it-down.faqs.0.question: How does this check if a site is down?
tools.is-it-down.faqs.0.answer: The tool requests the website through a public proxy. If the request succeeds, the site is reachable; if it fails, the site may be down.
tools.is-it-down.faqs.1.question: Why does it say 'might be down'?
tools.is-it-down.faqs.1.answer: Some sites block automated requests, and regional outages can differ. The result is a strong signal, not a guarantee.
tools.is-it-down.faqs.2.question: What should I do if my site is down?
tools.is-it-down.faqs.2.answer: Check your hosting provider's status page, look for DNS changes, and contact support if it stays down.

tools.is-it-down.guide.intro.title: What is Is It Down?
Is It Down checks whether a website is reachable right now, helping you tell if an outage affects everyone or just you.
tools.is-it-down.guide.sections.0.title: How to use it
tools.is-it-down.guide.sections.0.paragr: Enter the URL and click Check. The tool requests the site through a proxy and shows whether it responded.
A successful response means the site is up.
The status code and response time are shown for reference.
tools.is-it-down.guide.sections.1.title: Tips
tools.is-it-down.guide.sections.1.paragr: If a site is down for you but up here, the problem is likely on your side: your internet, DNS cache or local firewall.

tools.domain-age.faqs.0.question: Why does domain age matter?
tools.domain-age.faqs.0.answer: Older domains often appear more trustworthy to search engines and users, and expired-age domains may carry established history.
tools.domain-age.faqs.1.question: Where does the data come from?
tools.domain-age.faqs.1.answer: The tool reads the public RDAP registry data, the modern standard that replaced traditional WHOIS.
tools.domain-age.faqs.2.question: Can the registration date be hidden?
tools.domain-age.faqs.2.answer: Most registries publish registration dates publicly through RDAP. Privacy protection usually hides contact details, not dates.

tools.domain-age.guide.intro.title: What is a Domain Age Checker?
A domain age checker shows when a domain was registered and calculates how old it is in years, months and days.
tools.domain-age.guide.sections.0.title: How to use it
tools.domain-age.guide.sections.0.paragr: Enter a domain name (without http:// or www) and click Check. The registration, expiry and update dates are shown.
The age is calculated from the registration date.
Expiry and update dates are shown when available.
tools.domain-age.guide.sections.1.title: Tips
tools.domain-age.guide.sections.1.paragr: Use domain age when evaluating a site's history or deciding on a domain purchase.
tools.domain-hosting.metadata.title: Domain Hosting Checker
tools.domain-hosting.metadata.descriptio: Find out which hosting provider and network a domain uses
tools.domain-hosting.messages.errorInval: Please enter a valid domain name.
tools.domain-hosting.messages.errorNoARe: No A record was found for this domain. It may not be connected to a host yet.
tools.domain-hosting.messages.errorGener: Could not check this domain. Please try again.
tools.domain-hosting.faqs.0.question: How is hosting detected?
tools.domain-hosting.faqs.0.answer: The domain's A record is resolved to an IP address, then the network owner of that IP is looked up — that reveals the hosting provider.
tools.domain-hosting.faqs.1.question: What if the domain uses a CDN?
tools.domain-hosting.faqs.1.answer: If a CDN is in front, the IP belongs to the CDN (like Cloudflare) rather than the origin server. The tool will show the CDN as the host.
tools.domain-hosting.faqs.2.question: What is an ASN?
tools.domain-hosting.faqs.2.answer: An Autonomous System Number is a unique identifier for a network, typically an ISP, hosting provider or CDN.

tools.domain-hosting.guide.sections.0.pa: Enter a domain and click Check. The tool resolves the A record, then looks up the ISP and organization of the IP.
tools.domain-hosting.guide.sections.0.it: The result shows the IP address and its network owner.
ASN identifies the hosting provider or CDN.
tools.domain-hosting.guide.sections.1.pa: Knowing a competitor's hosting provider can help you compare performance options.

tools.xml-sitemap.messages.placeholder: Your generated sitemap will appear here.
tools.xml-sitemap.faqs.0.question: What is an XML sitemap?
tools.xml-sitemap.faqs.0.answer: An XML sitemap is a file that lists the important pages of your website so search engines can find and crawl them more efficiently.
tools.xml-sitemap.faqs.1.question: How often should I update my sitemap?
tools.xml-sitemap.faqs.1.answer: Update your sitemap whenever you add, remove, or change important pages. Most sites set the change frequency to weekly or monthly.
tools.xml-sitemap.faqs.2.question: Where should I upload the sitemap?
tools.xml-sitemap.faqs.2.answer: Upload sitemap.xml to the root of your website and submit it in Google Search Console or Bing Webmaster Tools.
tools.xml-sitemap.faqs.3.question: What priority should I use?
tools.xml-sitemap.faqs.3.answer: Priority ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 and tells search engines which pages are more important. Use 1.0 only for your homepage and key landing pages.

tools.xml-sitemap.guide.intro.paragraphs: An XML sitemap generator creates a sitemap.xml file that lists the URLs of your website, helping search engines discover and index your pages.
tools.xml-sitemap.guide.sections.0.title: How to use it
tools.xml-sitemap.guide.sections.0.parag: Enter your website URL, list the page paths (one per line), choose a change frequency and priority, then click Generate Sitemap.
tools.xml-sitemap.guide.sections.0.items: Paths can be absolute (/about) or relative (about).
The lastmod date is set to today automatically.

tools.adsense-calculator.metadata.title: Adsense Calculator
tools.adsense-calculator.metadata.descri: Estimate your Google AdSense revenue based on traffic and ad metrics
tools.adsense-calculator.messages.discla: Estimates only. Real earnings depend on niche, location, season, ad quality and many other factors.
tools.adsense-calculator.faqs.0.question: How is AdSense revenue calculated?
tools.adsense-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Earnings are roughly pageviews × ads per page × click-through rate (CTR) × cost per click (CPC). This tool uses that formula to give an estimate.
tools.adsense-calculator.faqs.1.question: What is a good CTR for AdSense?
tools.adsense-calculator.faqs.1.answer: A CTR between 1% and 3% is typical for display ads. High-quality, well-placed ads can perform better.
tools.adsense-calculator.faqs.2.question: What is CPC and what affects it?
tools.adsense-calculator.faqs.2.answer: CPC is the amount paid per click. It varies by niche, user location, season and advertiser competition.
tools.adsense-calculator.faqs.3.question: Why are the numbers only estimates?
tools.adsense-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Real earnings depend on many factors this calculator cannot know, such as traffic sources, ad quality and user behavior.
tools.adsense-calculator.guide.intro.par: An AdSense calculator estimates how much money your website can earn from Google AdSense based on your traffic and ad settings.
Enter your daily pageviews, the average number of ads per page, your click-through rate and cost per click. The daily, monthly and yearly estimates update instantly.
CTR is the percentage of ad impressions that get clicked.
CPC is the average amount you earn per click.
Use realistic values from your AdSense dashboard for better estimates.
Experiment with different inputs to see how traffic and engagement affect revenue.

tools.url-opener.messages.popupBlocked: Your browser blocked some pop-ups. Allow pop-ups for this site and try again.
tools.url-opener.faqs.0.question: Why does my browser block the tabs?
tools.url-opener.faqs.0.answer: Browsers block pop-ups triggered outside of a user gesture. If this happens, allow pop-ups for this site in your browser settings and try again.
tools.url-opener.faqs.1.question: Can I open URLs without http://?
tools.url-opener.faqs.1.answer: Yes. The tool automatically adds https:// to URLs that don't include a protocol.
tools.url-opener.faqs.2.question: How many URLs can I open?
tools.url-opener.faqs.2.answer: You can open as many as you like, but very large lists may be limited by your browser.

tools.url-opener.guide.intro.title: What is a URL Opener?
A URL opener lets you open many links at the same time in new tabs, saving you from copying and pasting each one individually.
tools.url-opener.guide.sections.0.title: How to use it
tools.url-opener.guide.sections.0.paragr: Paste your list of URLs (one per line or separated by commas), then click Open All URLs. Each URL opens in a new tab.
If the browser blocks tabs, allow pop-ups for this site.

tools.html-viewer.metadata.title: HTML Viewer
tools.html-viewer.metadata.description: View and preview HTML code in real time with syntax highlighting
tools.html-viewer.faqs.0.question: Does the preview run scripts?
tools.html-viewer.faqs.0.answer: The preview renders in a sandboxed iframe, so scripts are not executed for safety. Static HTML, CSS and inline styles work fully.
tools.html-viewer.faqs.1.question: Is my HTML sent anywhere?
tools.html-viewer.faqs.1.answer: No. Everything runs in your browser — your code never leaves your device.
tools.html-viewer.faqs.2.question: Can I copy the rendered output?
tools.html-viewer.faqs.2.answer: Use the Source tab to copy your HTML code, or the preview to check the visual result.

tools.html-viewer.guide.intro.title: What is an HTML Viewer?
tools.html-viewer.guide.intro.paragraphs: An HTML viewer renders your HTML code in real time so you can see the visual result while you edit.
tools.html-viewer.guide.sections.0.title: How to use it
tools.html-viewer.guide.sections.0.parag: Type or paste HTML into the editor on the left. The preview on the right updates automatically. Switch between Preview and Source tabs to inspect the rendered page or the code.

tools.mobile-friendly-test.metadata.desc: Check if your website is optimized for mobile devices
tools.mobile-friendly-test.messages.fetc: Could not fetch the page. The site may block automated requests or the URL may be invalid.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.messages.view: The page has a viewport meta tag set to device-width.
The page is missing a proper viewport meta tag.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.messages.titl: The page has a title tag.
The page has no title tag.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.messages.desc: The page has a meta description.
The page has no meta description.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.messages.resp: The page uses responsive CSS (media queries detected).
No media queries found — the layout may not adapt to small screens.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.messages.font: Legible font sizes (12px+) were detected in the CSS.
Font sizes are not clearly set; text may be hard to read on mobile.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.messages.disc: This is a lightweight heuristic check based on the page HTML. For a full analysis, use Google's official Mobile-Friendly Test.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.faqs.0.questi: How does the mobile friendly test work?
tools.mobile-friendly-test.faqs.0.answer: The tool fetches the page HTML and checks for common mobile optimizations: viewport meta tag, title, description, responsive CSS and font sizes.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.faqs.1.questi: What is a viewport meta tag?
tools.mobile-friendly-test.faqs.1.answer: A viewport meta tag like width=device-width tells mobile browsers to render the page at the device width instead of a desktop width.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.faqs.2.questi: Is this as accurate as Google's test?
tools.mobile-friendly-test.faqs.2.answer: No. This is a quick heuristic check. Google's Mobile-Friendly Test renders the page and provides a more complete evaluation.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.guide.intro.t: What is a Mobile Friendly Test?
tools.mobile-friendly-test.guide.intro.p: A mobile friendly test checks whether your website works well on phones and tablets, which is important for both user experience and Google's mobile-first indexing.
tools.mobile-friendly-test.guide.section: Enter the URL of the page you want to check and click Check URL. The tool fetches the page and shows a score with the checks it performed.
The score is based on the checks below it.
Fix failing checks to improve your mobile experience.
Start with the viewport meta tag — it is the most important single fix for mobile rendering.
